A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChronoDepth and share substantial methodological and experimental content. All 13 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v3 were inspected, including figures, equations, references and v3's appendices A–C. V1 contains no appendix; no material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original depth-estimation comparisons, ablations, depth-conditioned video-generation results and novel-view-synthesis experiments in Section 4.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark comparisons and ablations in Section 4, plus conditioning-noise sensitivity and additional qualitative results in the appendices.

M1.justification: V1 trains with one noise level per clip and repeatedly adds noise to overlapping depth predictions during temporal inpainting. V3 independently samples noise levels per frame during training and keeps overlapping predictions clean during inference, supplying a small conditioning noise level instead. The original inpainting procedure survives as the replacement-trick comparator; the sequential spatial/temporal training backbone remains.

E1.justification: V3 replaces MatrixCity evaluation with Sintel, adding explicitly dynamic synthetic scenes, and adds qualitative Bonn evaluation. TartanAir training expands from four indoor scenes to all 738 sequences. KITTI-360, ScanNet++ and the other training datasets remain. V1's depth-conditioned generation and novel-view-synthesis tasks are removed rather than relocated.

E2.justification: In the corresponding depth benchmark Table 1, v3 removes DPT and the separate Marigold without-ensemble variant, while adding DepthAnything V2, DepthCrafter and Marigold adapted from SVD. Marigold, DepthAnything and NVDS remain. Marigold (SVD) is a different comparator from v1's Marigold without ensemble.

E3.justification: Default inference overlap changes from one to five frames for ten-frame clips. V3 reports 90-frame ScanNet++ evaluation clips instead of v1's 200–240-frame description, adds optical-flow-based MFC* evaluation on Sintel and average benchmark rankings, and specifies a ten-frame/five-overlap configuration for DepthCrafter. Training-factor ablations now use naive inference as their common control. Renaming Sim. to MFC does not itself change the retained pose-warping metric.

E4.justification: The three training-factor ablations remain and extend to ScanNet++, but inference analysis expands to naive, replacement-trick and consistent-context strategies, with temporal-slice comparisons in Figure 6. V1's overlap-length sensitivity study disappears. V3 Appendix B and Figure S1 introduce a distinct sensitivity study of the conditioning noise level.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. V3's discussion of uncertainty in previous depth predictions concerns its conditioning mechanism, not statistical reporting of experimental results.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation values are substantially replaced. Expressed as fractions, v1's KITTI-360 ChronoDepth AbsRel/δ1 results of 0.196/0.724 are replaced by 0.215/0.654 in v3 under revised settings, so this is not a controlled performance comparison. V3 adds Sintel, new-comparator and conditioning-noise results; MatrixCity scores, generation FID/FVD results and novel-view-synthesis convergence results disappear.

T1.justification: V3 extends the retained EDM/DSM formulation to independently sampled frame-specific noise vectors and explicitly formulates noisy versus clean overlap conditioning in Section 3.2. No theorem or proof is added. There is also a mathematical reporting discrepancy: v1 samples noise with covariance sigma squared times I, whereas v3 Equations 1 and 9 multiply standard Gaussian noise by sigma squared, unlike Equation 8's sigma multiplier.

C1.justification: The principal contribution shifts toward consistent context-aware training and inference for streamed videos. V1's highlighted one-frame overlap tradeoff and demonstrated benefits for video generation and novel-view synthesis disappear from the abstract, introduction and conclusion. The overarching claim of superior temporal consistency with comparable spatial accuracy remains.

C2.justification: V1 presents noisy temporal inpainting as effective; v3 interprets the matched replacement trick as providing fluctuating context that leaves cross-clip inconsistency. V3 adds explanations involving accumulated prediction errors and small conditioning noise, discusses streaming restrictions and argues for temporal consistency despite weaker Sintel AbsRel. Its claim that sequential training always improves consistency conflicts with KITTI-360 Table 2 rows C/D, where MFC changes from 0.482 to 0.505.

D1.justification: Core optimizer, resolution, training budgets and hardware disclosures remain. V3 adds inference pseudocode, exact evaluation selections, global per-video scale/shift alignment and invalid-pixel masking, and changes the project-page address. These disclosures do not establish that previously unspecified procedures changed. Runtime, memory-capacity and ensemble details are removed. Appendix B specifies sigma epsilon = 4, inconsistent with Figure S1's negative-valued axis, leaving the new parameter unclear.

R1.justification: V1 positions itself as the first adaptation of video diffusion to consistent depth estimation and motivates inpainting through RePaint. V3 acknowledges concurrent DepthCrafter, credits Diffusion Forcing as inspiration and distinguishes its contribution through consistent context conditioning and streaming requirements. It adds relevant infinite-video and newer depth literature; RePaint and references supporting the removed generation/NVS experiments disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around within-clip and cross-clip context. Method exposition is reorganized into naive formulation, consistent context-aware strategy and multi-stage training, while the experimental narrative is rewritten and the applications section removed. Related-work headings are streamlined, appendices are introduced and the author/affiliation block changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. V3 adds a front-page teaser and inference-strategy illustration, redraws the matched training/inference diagrams, and presents three adjacent algorithms. Tables gain new grouping, ranking columns and ablation controls. Qualitative displays incorporate temporal slices, while application figures and the overlap plot are replaced by inference and appendix displays.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the central evaluation with direct inference-strategy comparisons, additional baselines, dynamic Sintel scenes and temporal-slice visualizations, while narrowing the paper by removing application and runtime evidence. However, its new conditioning parameter conflicts with Figure S1, its noise equations are inconsistent, and an ablation interpretation contradicts Table 2. These problems affect verification of the revised method and its supporting argument, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
